cues.subtitle: Hub is a bank; Alice, Bob and Carol are its customers. Each registers as an entity on the Depository contract, controlled by its own signing board.
cues.title: A bank and three customers join the Depository
cues.tradfiParallel: Participants admitted to the settlement system before any business.
cues.what: Hub is a bank; Alice, Bob and Carol are its customers. Each registers as an entity on the Depository contract, controlled by its own signing board.
cues.why: This part follows one bank failure to the end: who is paid, from what, and in which order.

cues.subtitle: Hub holds 350,000 USDC of test balance as reserve on the Depository. The customers hold none.
cues.title: Hub's capital is credited on the Depository
cues.tradfiParallel: Settled in the Depository's settlement asset (here a USDC test token; in a central bank deployment, tokenised reserves).
cues.what: Hub holds 350,000 USDC of test balance as reserve on the Depository. The customers hold none.
cues.why: A reserve is what the Depository pays a bank's obligations from when the bank itself does not.

cues.subtitle: Alice, Bob and Carol each open a bilateral account with Hub and grant Hub a 500,000 USDC credit line: Hub may owe each of them that much without collateral.
cues.title: Each customer opens an account with Hub
cues.tradfiParallel: A deposit account: the depositor lends to the bank up to an amount it chooses.
cues.what: Alice, Bob and Carol each open a bilateral account with Hub and grant Hub a 500,000 USDC credit line: Hub may owe each of them that much without collateral.
cues.why: The customer, not the bank, sets how much unsecured exposure it accepts. The limit caps its loss.

cues.subtitle: Hub moves its whole 350,000 USDC reserve into its account with Carol as collateral. Hub's reserve is now empty.
cues.title: Carol asks for security: Hub posts collateral
cues.tradfiParallel: Pledged collateral held at the settlement system, segregated for one counterparty.
cues.what: Hub moves its whole 350,000 USDC reserve into its account with Carol as collateral. Hub's reserve is now empty.
cues.why: Collateral sits in the Depository, locked to one account. Only that account's counterparty can be paid from it.

cues.subtitle: Hub pays 200,000 USDC to Alice, 150,000 USDC to Bob, 100,000 USDC to Carol inside their accounts. Each payment is co-signed by both sides.
cues.title: Hub credits its customers
cues.tradfiParallel: Deposits: each balance is the bank's liability to its customer.
cues.what: Hub pays 200,000 USDC to Alice, 150,000 USDC to Bob, 100,000 USDC to Carol inside their accounts. Each payment is co-signed by both sides.
cues.why: Every co-signed state is a claim on Hub that its holder can take to the Depository alone.

cues.subtitle: Alice: 200,000 USDC (0 USDC covered by collateral); Bob: 150,000 USDC (0 USDC covered by collateral); Carol: 100,000 USDC (100,000 USDC covered by collateral). Hub's reserve is empty.
cues.title: Starting point: Hub owes three customers
cues.tradfiParallel: A bank with one secured and two unsecured creditors and no liquid assets left.
cues.what: Alice: 200,000 USDC (0 USDC covered by collateral); Bob: 150,000 USDC (0 USDC covered by collateral); Carol: 100,000 USDC (100,000 USDC covered by collateral). Hub's reserve is empty.
cues.why: Only Carol is secured. Alice and Bob rely on credit: if Hub fails they are paid from Hub's reserve, and what the reserve cannot pay becomes on-chain debt.

cues.subtitle: Alice freezes its account with Hub and drafts a dispute from the last state both signed.
cues.title: Hub stops responding: Alice exits alone
cues.tradfiParallel: Close-out on the last confirmed position, without the defaulting party.
cues.what: Alice freezes its account with Hub and drafts a dispute from the last state both signed.
cues.why: Exit needs no cooperation from the failed bank: the last co-signed state is the evidence.

cues.subtitle: Alice submits the dispute to the Depository. Hub has 25 hours to answer with a newer co-signed state; the demo fast-forwards the clock.
cues.title: Alice's dispute is filed: the challenge window opens
cues.tradfiParallel: A claim with a fixed contest period.
cues.what: Alice submits the dispute to the Depository. Hub has 25 hours to answer with a newer co-signed state; the demo fast-forwards the clock.
cues.why: An older state loses only if the other side answers in time with a newer one, so each bank — or a watchtower — must watch the chain during the window.

cues.subtitle: No newer state arrived. Alice's runtime submits the finalization on its own.
cues.title: Alice's window closes: finalization submitted
cues.tradfiParallel: The contest period lapses and the claim becomes enforceable.
cues.what: No newer state arrived. Alice's runtime submits the finalization on its own.
cues.why: A deadline, not a negotiation, ends the dispute.

cues.subtitle: The Depository applied the last co-signed state. Hub's reserve was empty, so the whole 200,000 USDC is booked on-chain as Hub's debt to Alice, behind nobody.
cues.title: Alice's claim becomes Hub's debt, number 1 in the queue
cues.tradfiParallel: The Depository applies the latest co-signed state mechanically; legal finality depends on governing law. How the on-chain queue ranks in insolvency is a legal question.
cues.what: The Depository applied the last co-signed state. Hub's reserve was empty, so the whole 200,000 USDC is booked on-chain as Hub's debt to Alice, behind nobody.
cues.why: Debts are paid first-come, not pro rata: the oldest claim is paid in full before the next one receives anything. While any debt is open, the debtor cannot move reserve out; every outflow pays the queue first.

cues.why: Exit needs no cooperation from the failed bank: the last co-signed state is the evidence.

cues.subtitle: The Depository paid Carol 100,000 USDC from the account's collateral. The remaining 250,000 USDC of collateral belonged to Hub and went to Hub's reserve, where the debt queue has the first claim on it.
cues.title: Carol is paid from collateral; the surplus returns to Hub's reserve
cues.tradfiParallel: The Depository applies the latest co-signed state mechanically; legal finality depends on governing law.
cues.what: The Depository paid Carol 100,000 USDC from the account's collateral. The remaining 250,000 USDC of collateral belonged to Hub and went to Hub's reserve, where the debt queue has the first claim on it.
cues.why: Collateral protected Carol fully. Hub still owes 350,000 USDC, so it cannot move that reserve out.

cues.subtitle: A call to the Depository's debt enforcement pays Hub's queue from Hub's reserve, oldest debt first. It needs no signature from Hub; the demo submits it.
cues.title: Anyone triggers debt enforcement
cues.tradfiParallel: Execution of claims against a defaulter's settlement account, in order of filing.
cues.what: A call to the Depository's debt enforcement pays Hub's queue from Hub's reserve, oldest debt first. It needs no signature from Hub; the demo submits it.
cues.why: Enforcement is permissionless and can only move money from the debtor to its creditors, in queue order.

cues.subtitle: Alice received 200,000 USDC, paid in full; Bob received 50,000 USDC and is still owed 100,000 USDC. Hub's reserve is 0 USDC.
cues.title: The queue is paid first-come
cues.tradfiParallel: Strict priority by time of claim, not a pro rata distribution.
cues.what: Alice received 200,000 USDC, paid in full; Bob received 50,000 USDC and is still owed 100,000 USDC. Hub's reserve is 0 USDC.
cues.why: Debts are paid first-come, not pro rata: the oldest claim is paid in full before the next one receives anything. While any debt is open, the debtor cannot move reserve out; every outflow pays the queue first.

cues.subtitle: 150,000 USDC arrives in Hub's reserve (a test credit here; in practice fresh capital or a repaid loan).
cues.title: New money reaches Hub's reserve
cues.tradfiParallel: Recoveries flowing into the estate are applied to outstanding claims.
cues.what: 150,000 USDC arrives in Hub's reserve (a test credit here; in practice fresh capital or a repaid loan).
cues.why: Every future inflow to the debtor's reserve is caught by the queue before the debtor can use it.

cues.subtitle: A call to the Depository's debt enforcement pays Hub's queue from Hub's reserve, oldest debt first. It needs no signature from Hub; the demo submits it.
cues.title: Debt enforcement runs again
cues.tradfiParallel: Execution of claims against a defaulter's settlement account, in order of filing.
cues.what: A call to the Depository's debt enforcement pays Hub's queue from Hub's reserve, oldest debt first. It needs no signature from Hub; the demo submits it.
cues.why: Enforcement is permissionless and can only move money from the debtor to its creditors, in queue order.

cues.subtitle: Enforcement paid Bob the remaining 100,000 USDC. Hub owes nothing on-chain, and the rest of its reserve, 50,000 USDC, is free again.
cues.title: Bob is made whole; the queue is empty
cues.tradfiParallel: All claims satisfied in order of priority; the remainder returns to the debtor.
cues.what: Enforcement paid Bob the remaining 100,000 USDC. Hub owes nothing on-chain, and the rest of its reserve, 50,000 USDC, is free again.
cues.why: Every customer was paid in full: Carol from collateral, Alice and Bob from the queue as reserves came in. The order was set by the chain, not by Hub.
